result.summary: Design doc r4 for STRAT-AGENT-BG-WRITE-1 is complete and committed (64ab0e3). Addresses the sole remaining design-gate r3 finding: terminal sentinel writes were not serialized — the error handler and exit handler could both pass their own no-sentinel check and each append a sentinel, with scanStream() taking the last one (timing-dependent outcome). Fix: added `finalizationClaim: Promise<void> | null` to `ClaudeBgEntry` plus a `claimFinalization()` helper that is the single serialization point for all terminal writes. The null-check + set is synchronous at the JS event-loop level, so the first path to fire (error before exit on worker exceptions) atomically claims the lock and the exit handler discards its own doFinalize. Cancel path routes through claimFinalization() in both the rescan-won and cancel-owned branches, guarding concurrent cancel calls. Registry deletion always happens in .finally() — exactly once per run. Added D13 decision and 5 new test cases covering the serialization invariant. No other sections changed from r3.

result.summary: Design r5 for STRAT-AGENT-BG-WRITE-1 committed (2dfe058). Addresses the sole r4 finding: a cancel that joins a pre-existing error/exit finalizationClaim unconditionally returned 'cancelled' while the committed sentinel was rc=1 — cancel/poll disagreement. Fix (D14): before calling claimFinalization(rc=130), check entry.finalizationClaim !== null. If non-null, we joined rather than owned — await the existing claim, rescan, return already_complete/already_error per the actual committed sentinel. Return 'cancelled' only when finalizationClaim was null at the check (we own the rc=130 record). The null-check + set is atomic at the JS event-loop level. Added D14 to the decision log and 3 new test cases: (1) cancel joins error claim → returns already_error with matching poll; (2) cancel owns rc=130 → still returns 'cancelled'; (3) concurrent second cancel joins first cancel's claim correctly. No other sections changed from r4.
